study_identification_part.si_4_title: Closing the life-cycle of normative modeling using federated hierarchical Bayesian regression

dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.detail: Table 1 lists 16 datasets: ABCD, CAMCAN, CMI (HBN), CNP (UCLA-LA5c), FCON, HCP (HCP-YA), HCPAG (HCP-A), HCPDV (HCP-D), HCPEP (HCP-EP), IXI, NKI, OASIS3 (OASIS-3), OPN (OpenNeuro), PNC, TOP, and UKBB (UK Biobank). OPN is listed as OpenNeuro in references but not in the guidance table, hence mapped to 'Unknown'.
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.supporting_text: Table 1 lists the 16 neuroimaging datasets that are used in our experiments... ABCD... CAMCAN... CMI... CNP... FCON... HCP... HCPAG... HCPDV... HCPEP... IXI... NKI... OASIS3... OPN... PNC... TOP... UKBB
dc_1_datasets_using_in_this_study.location: Kia2022.pdf.md: Materials and methods / Datasets and preprocessing / Table 1

dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.detail: The study uses 12 datasets for estimating the reference normative model and 4 clinical datasets (CNP, HCPEP, OASIS3, TOP) for model adaptation and clinical evaluation of deviations.
dc_2_purpose_of_each_dataset.supporting_text: we first use a linear homoscedastic model to estimate the parameters of the reference normative model on datasets with only healthy participants (ABCD, CAMCAN, CMI, FCON, HCP, HCPAG, HCPDV, IXI, NKI OPN, PNC, and UKBB). Then, in each run 50% of random healthy participants in clinical datasets, including CNP, HCPEP, OASIS3, and TOP are used to recalibrate the parameters of the reference model.

dc_3_number_of_healthy_control_of_each_n.detail: The total number of healthy controls across all 16 datasets is 36,019 (37,126 total scans minus 1,107 patients). For the multi-site regression experiment, 80% of healthy samples were used for training.

dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.detail: The age range of the pooled dataset is 6-100 years. Mean and SD are not explicitly reported for the overall healthy sample or the train set. Min/Max for the train phase are inferred to be the same due to random sampling of 80% of the data.
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.confidence_rating: High for Min/Max, Low for Mean/SD
dc_4_age_info_of_each_normative_nodel.supporting_text: The final data consists of 37126 scans from 79 scanners that reasonably cover a wide range of human lifespan from 6 to 100 years old. Fig 5 depicts the age span for each dataset.
